key_insight: A compatible space–time FEM can enforce exact discrete energy conservation for rotating shallow water dynamics, including stochastic forcing, by using projected auxiliary Hamiltonian variables.
engineering_relevance: This offers a high-fidelity, structure-preserving solver strategy for geophysical flow simulations where long-time stability and conservation are critical.
method: Space–time finite elements with compatible FE spaces in space and continuous Petrov–Galerkin time discretization.
Projected auxiliary variables are introduced to preserve the Hamiltonian energy exactly.
A monolithic patch-smoother iterative solver is used to make Newton solves accurate enough that solver-induced energy drift stays very small.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests demonstrating convergence, conservation, and robustness for both deterministic and stochastic formulations.
watch_item: Exact conservation depends on sufficiently converged nonlinear solves and the added complexity of projected auxiliary variables and monolithic patch smoothing.
paper_title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
